text:
Carla: Heads-up — noticed an old service key in a public gist referencing 'redwood-staging-s3'. It looks like a long-lived GCP sa key that was uploaded last week. Not yet clear if it was used.
Alex: Ugh. Do we have proof of access? any logs? :eyes:
Mike: Checked Cloud Audit logs briefly — a handful of reads from that service-account within the last 48h, from a CI worker IP. Could be CI leaking an env var. I can attach a short grep later.
Carla: Ok immediate plan: 1) revoke the exposed key 2) rotate CI secret -> use Vault wrapped GCP key 3) run quick scan for other public gists. Who can revoke now?
Dan: I can revoke the key from GCP now. Will also block token issuance for that SA. Doing it in 2m and will paste command.
SRE-Oncall: If you revoke, please also remove access in RBAC binding for that SA on the bucket — prevents any new tokens from working as a fallback. I'll handle RBAC change.
Dan: Revoking now: ```gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete 0123abcd --iam-account=ci-sa@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com``` Result: SUCCESS. Also disabled key.
VaultBot: [vault] Detected a stale GCP key reference in secret path secret/data/ci/gcp/key-id=0123abcd. Recommend rotating wrapped_key and re-wrapping with KMS.
Mike: For CI: switch to short-lived impersonation via Workload Identity + Vault GCP plugin. Can we target a quick rollout to staging first?
Carla: Yes staging first. @Liz can you coordinate CI job changes? We need env var update and deploy window.
Liz: On it — will open a PR to replace GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS with VAULT_GCP_IMPERSONATE config and add rollout notes. Targeting staging deploy in 90m.
Security-Bot: Audit rule triggered: public gist containing 'redwood' matched regex for credentials. Creating incident ticket SEC-4321 and bookmarking logs. Also flagging for leak search across github.com and pastebin.
Alex: Two follow-ups: a) run `git grep` across repos for the key id b) run automated gist search script I have (will post results). Expect ~30m.
Mike: Also recommend we rotate any downstream AWS KMS-wrapped secrets that used the SA for encryption. If objects were encrypted using a key protected by SA, we need to re-wrap. Suggest runbook step: list dependent resources, re-encrypt with new key version.
Carla: Good point. We're using GCP KMS for some artifacts and AWS KMS for others. We'll do key re-wraps where SA had encrypt/decrypt perms.
Dan: Notes on Vault side: rotate the secret version and update CI path. Example API call to create new version: ```curl -sS -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" -X POST https://vault.internal/v1/secret/data/ci/gcp -d '{"data": {"key_id": "<new>", "wrapped_key":"<wrapped>"}}'``` Also ensure the vault role uses KMS transit key for wrapping.
SRE-Oncall: RBAC change done: removed roles/storage.objectViewer from that SA on the staging bucket. Propagation confirmed.
Liz: PR merged for CI change, kicking staging run now. If staging tests pass, will roll to prod after 1h.
Alex: Scan results: found 2 other gists referencing a staging token string pattern. One is expired; other looked active but from same CI worker. Marked in SEC-4321.
Carla: Assignments: Dan — rotate GCP keys and post new key IDs to Vault; Mike — check KMS re-wraps and list impacted artifacts; Liz — deploy CI changes & update runbook; Alex — finish leak search and post findings; SRE-Oncall — RBAC removals and confirm audit trails. ETA 3h for full rotation.
Security-Bot: Logging actions:
- key revoke by Dan @ 1752009940
- RBAC edit by SRE-Oncall @ 1752010200
- Vault write by Dan @ 1752010800
Incident ticket SEC-4321 updated.
Carla: Also quick note — let's add an audit alert on Vault paths for any write that changes wrapped_key fields. We should have that monitored.
VaultBot: Rule suggestion: alert when secret/data/* includes "wrapped_key" changes and origin IP is external. Can wire to PagerDuty.
Liz: Staging passed. Rolling to prod in 30m. Will post deploy ts.
SRE-Oncall: Confirmed no suspicious egress after key revoke. Network logs show only CI host talk stopped. Good.
Carla: Great work team. We'll debrief in incident postmortem doc and add a control to block long-lived SA keys in CI. Closing thread when SEC-4321 PM confirms closure. :white_check_mark:
